title: Arignar Anna and the Rajya Sabha Window Metaphor: Why Shut Out the Fresh Breeze?
summary: In the 1963 Rajya Sabha language debate, Arignar Anna delivered a celebrated oratorical masterstroke using the metaphor of a window to argue for international scientific openness.
keywords: Historical Dialogue 141: காந்தியும் ராஜாஜியும்: “குறும்பான கடிதம்” என்ற விமர்சனத்துக்கு பதில்
full_text:
In May 1963, the Rajya Sabha was engulfed in a heated debate over the Official Languages Bill. Several members passionately argued that English, as a relic of foreign colonial subjugation, should be summarily expelled from Indian public administration.

Rising to speak from the opposition benches, C. N. Annadurai addressed the House in measured, resonant prose:
"Mr. Chairman, Sir, my esteemed friends argue that English is a foreign tongue and must be banished forthwith. I do not dispute its foreign origin. But let us reflect upon a simple domestic truth.

India is our ancestral home. Its doors must remain wide open to our own indigenous mother tongues. But why, in our haste, should we shut the windows?
English is an international window through which the fresh, invigorating breeze of modern science, technological progress, and global thought enters our home! If you slam that window shut out of misplaced pride, you will plunge this house into intellectual suffocation and stagnation. In an interconnected world, we need that window wide open so our young minds can soar across the globe!"

The visual power of the 'window metaphor' electrified the chamber, drawing applause from across the political spectrum and permanently elevating the national discourse on linguistic federalism.
